title: Slovenia Bomber Crew Memorial
narrative: During the Second World War, approximately 500 Allied aircraft were lost over Slovenian territory, primarily from the 15th US Air Force operating out of Italy. By 1946, the remains of more than 100 Allied pilots had been exhumed and returned to their hometowns or military cemeteries. Multiple crash site memorials have since been established across Slovenia to commemorate these crews.
contributor: Keith Binley, Bomber Command Memorial Register

external_narratives.summary: US War Memorials entry for the B-17 'Dark Eyes' (41-24405) crash site memorial at Andraz nad Polzelo, Slovenia. Eight crew from the 96th BS, 2nd BG, 15th Air Force were killed on 19 March 1944 when shot down during a raid on Klagenfurt, Austria. Memorial stone unveiled 2014.

memorial_details:
Inauguration of B-17 Dark Eyes Memorial (April 8, 1917): The memorial was inaugurated to commemorate the service and sacrifice of ten brave Americans from the crew of B-17F Dark Eyes (41-24405). The keynote was made by US Senator and Vietnam Veteran Pilot, John McCain.

Dedication of B-17 Je Reviens (44-6437) Crash Site Memorial (March 11, 2017): The memorial was dedicated to commemorate the crash of B-17G Je Reviens (44-6437) on March 9, 1945. The ceremony included a keynote speech by Ambassador Hartley from the US Embassy Slovenia.
